chunks: A man asked al-Sadiq عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Allah destroys usury and gives increase to charities.

Yet I see one who consumes usury and his wealth increases. So he said: What destruction is more destructive than a dirham of usury that destroys religion? Then if he repents from it, his wealth goes away and he becomes poor.

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury; unlawful increase in financial transactions
key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتِ: charities; acts of giving for Allah's sake
key_terms.تَابَ: he repented and turned back from the sin
key_terms.يَمْحَقُ: He obliterates or removes blessing and lasting benefit
key_terms.يُرْبِي: He causes to grow and increase with blessing

ai.seo_question: How does Allah destroy riba if the wealth of those who deal in usury appears to increase?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the destruction mentioned in the verse is not limited to visible financial loss, but includes the ruin of a person's religion through riba. It also indicates that the apparent growth of wealth through usury is not true blessing, and repentance may result in the loss of such unlawfully gained wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4005 - A man asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the saying of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic:
"Allah (swt) destroys usury and gives increase for charities." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:276).
He asked: "Yet I see those who consume usury, and their wealth increases."
Imam (as) replied: "Is there any destruction greater than a dirham of usury that destroys one's religion? If he repents from it, his wealth will vanish, and he will become poor."
